value.rationale: The nonconstant quantum Gibbs metric presents a physically motivated setting where enforcing equal thermodynamic arc-length increases the full quadratic stochastic cost, with a computable limiting 11.07% gap. The positive-noise optimal schedule is metric-independent and the integer-grid asymptotic shows the allocation survives finite-count optimization, enabling a clear design rule for weak-noise quench experiments. This is more than a detached inequality or an arbitrarily chosen finite parameter calculation.
